blocks.md: **Fixed effects lets every individual have her own intercept while the slopes stay common, so all permanent, unmeasured differences between people are controlled for. It can be estimated by adding a dummy for each person, or, more practically, by subtracting each person's own averages from her data, which removes the intercepts altogether. Both give the same slopes. An $F$ test of equal intercepts strongly rejects pooling in the wage panel.**

blocks.title: Source
blocks.md: Section 4 of `Regression_Lecture5.ipynb` and section 3 of its mathematical appendix (see [Econ 430 L23 Panel Data and Microeconomic Panels](note:econ-430-l23-panel-data-and-microeconomic-panels) for how the notebook maps to lectures). Data: the NLS wage panel of [Econ 430 L24 The Pooled Panel Model](note:econ-430-l24-the-pooled-panel-model).

The most general model lets every coefficient differ by individual, $y_{it} = \beta_{1i} + \beta_{2i}x_{2it} + \beta_{3i}x_{3it} + e_{it}$. The popular simplification keeps the slopes common and lets only the intercepts differ:

All behavioural differences between individuals, *individual heterogeneity*, are captured by the intercept, which controls for individual-specific, time-invariant characteristics. This is the **fixed effects model**, and the $\beta_{1i}$ are the fixed effects ([Fixed Effects Regression](note:fixed-effects-regression)).

sections.heading: 2. The least squares dummy variable estimator

blocks.md: Define a dummy $D_{ji} = 1$ if $i = j$ for each of the $N$ individuals and estimate, with no common intercept,

by OLS: the **least squares dummy variable (LSDV)** estimator. Whether the intercepts differ is the joint test $H_0\!: \beta_{11} = \cdots = \beta_{1N}$, $N - 1$ restrictions; the restricted model is the pooled one ([F Test of Joint Hypotheses](note:f-test-of-joint-hypotheses)):
For the first 10 women ($NT = 50$), $\ln(WAGE)$ on experience, tenure (each with its square) and union: $SSE_R = 5.5025$, $SSE_U = 2.6672$, $J = 9$ and $NT - K = 50 - 15 = 35$.

blocks.prompt: Compute the $F$ statistic for equal intercepts across the 10 women.

wrong.md: that leaves out the division by $J = 9$ in the numerator
that is the ratio $SSE_R/SSE_U - 1$, without the degrees-of-freedom scaling

blocks.why: $F = \frac{(5.5025 - 2.6672)/9}{2.6672/35} = \frac{0.3150}{0.0762} = 4.134$, with $p = 0.0011$ on $F(9, 35)$: the intercepts differ, and the data should not be pooled into one model with a common intercept.

blocks.md: To see the dummies at work, the notebook fits the simpler $\ln(WAGE) = \beta_{1i} + \beta_2EXPER + e$ for the same 10 women: a common slope of 0.049 per year of experience, and intercepts from 1.25 to 1.98. Each woman gets a parallel line; the single pooled line (black) cuts across them.

blocks.title: Correction to the lecture notebook
blocks.md: In the text of the LSDV example the restricted model reads $\ldots + \beta_4TENURE + \beta_3TENURE^2 + \beta_6UNION$; the tenure-squared coefficient is $\beta_5$. The unrestricted model's "$\beta_{1N}\sum_{N=1}^{10}D_{Ni}$" stands for the ten separate terms $\beta_{11}D_{1i} + \cdots + \beta_{1,10}D_{10,i}$, each with its own coefficient.
With thousands of individuals, LSDV needs thousands of dummies. Instead, average individual $i$'s equation over her $T$ periods (the parameters do not change over time):
and subtract it from the original, term by term. The intercept cancels:

blocks.tex: \tilde y_{it} = y_{it} - \bar y_i = \beta_2\tilde x_{2it} + \beta_3\tilde x_{3it} + \tilde e_{it} .

blocks.md: OLS on these deviations from individual means is the **fixed effects (within) estimator**; it gives the same slopes as LSDV. The intercepts are recovered afterwards, because the fitted regression passes through each individual's means:

blocks.tex: b_{1i} = \bar y_i - b_2\bar x_{2i} - b_3\bar x_{3i}, \qquad i = 1, \dots, N .

blocks.md: For the 10 women the within estimator reproduces the LSDV slopes exactly (experience 0.238, tenure $-0.012$, union 0.114) and the estimated effects equal the dummy coefficients (0.152 for woman 1, 0.187 for woman 2, $-0.063$ for woman 3).

blocks.title: Correction to the lecture notebook
blocks.md: The recovered effect is written $b_{1i} = \bar y - b_2\bar x_{2i} - b_3\bar x_{3i}$; the first term is the individual's own mean $\bar y_i$, not the overall mean.

blocks.prompt: In the NLS wage panel, a woman's race (black) and her years of schooling do not change across the five waves. What happens to their coefficients in the within estimator?

options.feedback: Their deviations from the individual means are zero in every period, so they carry no within variation.

options.md: They cannot be estimated: demeaning turns them into columns of zeros, and their effects are absorbed into the fixed effects
They are estimated, but with larger standard errors
options.feedback: There is no variation at all to estimate them from, not just less.
The intercepts absorb their effects along with every other permanent difference, but cannot separate them.

blocks.why: $x_{kit} - \bar x_{ki} = 0$ whenever $x_{ki}$ is constant over time. Fixed effects controls for every time-invariant trait, measured or not, at the price of not estimating any of their effects ([Econ 430 L29 The Hausman-Taylor Estimator](note:econ-430-l29-the-hausman-taylor-estimator) addresses this).

blocks.md: On all 716 women, the test of equal intercepts (the "pooled $F$" of the within regression) gives $F = 20.87$ on $F(715, 2859)$, $p \approx 0$: fixed effects add a great deal beyond pooled OLS.

blocks.prompt: Where do the degrees of freedom $F(715, 2859)$ come from in the full-panel test?

options.md: $715 = N - 1$ restrictions; $2859 = NT - N - 5$ residual degrees of freedom for 716 intercepts and 5 slopes

options.feedback: $T = 5$, so $T - 1 = 4$; the restrictions equate the 716 individual intercepts.

options.md: $715$ is the number of regressors and $2859$ the number of observations
options.feedback: There are 3,580 observations and 5 slopes; the numerator counts restrictions.

options.md: Both come from the pooled model
options.feedback: The denominator uses the unrestricted (fixed effects) model's residuals.

blocks.why: Equal intercepts for 716 women is 715 restrictions. The fixed effects model estimates 716 intercepts and 5 slopes from 3,580 observations: $3{,}580 - 716 - 5 = 2{,}859$.
